proof_summary: Lucas-type binomial congruences pair the two halves of each defining sum to show that the relevant values at \(p+r\) vanish for \(0\le r<p-1\); at \(p-1\), they give \(a(p-1)=1\), while vanishing central binomial coefficients leave only the middle term and give \(c(p-1)=(-1)^{(p-1)/2}\). Thus both Hankel matrices are anti-triangular modulo \(p\); reversing the columns and combining the reversal sign \((-1)^{p(p-1)/2}\) with the anti-diagonal products yields the two determinant congruences.
